newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chronology of events in Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of events in Chechnya.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Chechnya's leader Alsan Maskhadov signed a peace deal on Monday which they said put an end to 400 years of confrontation between Moscow and the north Caucausus region.
Here is a history of the region and of the two-year conflict with troops sent there by Russia to crush the independence bid.
1859 - The Moslem North Caucasus region of Chechnya is incorporated into the Russian empire after nearly half a century of fighting led by legendary Imam Shamil.
1944 - Soviet dictator Josef Stalin deports the entire Chechen people to Central Asia, accusing them of collaboration with Nazi Germany. Tens of thousands die.
1957 - Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev allows the Chechens back to the Caucasus, setting up the Checheno-Ingush republic.
Oct 1991 - Following the overthrow of local communist ruler Doku Zavgayev, Soviet air force general Dzhokhar Dudayev wins a disputed local poll and declares Chechnya independent.
Russia rejects any talk of independence but takes no action against Dudayev and allows him to run Chechnya.
Summer/Autumn 1994 - Russia says Dudayev is letting Chechnya become a haven for terrorists. Moscow gives military support to the anti-Dudayev opposition but an assault on Grozny fails.
Dec 1994 - President Boris Yeltsin sends troops to Chechnya to crush the independence movement, but they meet strong resistance from guerrilla fighters and suffer heavy casualties.
Feb 1995 - Separatists abandon Grozny, reduced to ruins by tank, artillery and rocket attacks over a month of fighting.
June 1995 - Rebels seize hundreds of hostages in the Russian town of Budennovsk. Over 100 people die. Peace talks open, Russia orders a halt to military operations, but the conflict goes on.
Dec 1995 - Moscow-backed leader Zavgayev wins polls to head Chechnya's administration, amid reports of massive electoral fraud.
Jan 1996 - Fighters seize hostages in neighbouring Dagestan, then move to the village of Pervomaiskoye just outside Chechnya. Most rebels escape, but many are killed.
Feb 1996 - Yeltsin says the Chechnya campaign was "maybe one of our mistakes". He rules out withdrawal of Russian forces or massive use of force.

March 1996 - Rebels attack Grozny and hold some areas for several days. Yeltsin announces a halt to wide-scale military action, a partial withdrawal of troops and an offer of indirect talks with the rebels. The fighting continues.
April 1996 - Dudayev is killed in a rocket attack and replaced by vice-president Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev.
May 1996 - Yeltsin and Yandarbiyev agree a truce at talks in Moscow. It holds until the presidential poll which Yeltsin wins some six weeks later. Yeltsin visits Russian troops in Grozny.

Aug 1996 - Rebels seize Grozny. Yeltsin gives national security adviser Alexander Lebed powers to resolve the crisis. Lebed signs a truce on August 31 providing for a Russian pullout and deferring the issue of Chechen sovereignty for five years.
Sept 1996 - Russia starts withdrawing its soldiers.
Oct 1996 - Aslan Maskhadov, former rebel chief-of-staff, is named prime minister of an interim government. His platform includes independence and some elements of Islamic sharia law.
Nov 23, 1996 - Maskhadov and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin sign a treaty on principles of relations between Russia and Chechnya pending the presidential poll in Chechnya.
Dec 1996 - Six foreign Red Cross workers are murdered in Chechnya, casting a shadow over the election campaign.
Jan 1997 - Last Russian troops leave. Thirteen candidates run for president on January 27 and Maskhadov is elected with almost 65 percent of the vote.
Jan 1997 - Unidentified kidnappers seize two Russian journalists in Chechnya, first in a series of incidents which escalate tensions in the region.
Feb 12, 1997 - Maskhadov takes his oath of office.
Feb 21, 1997 - Negotiations start between Moscow and the Chechen government to draft a peace accord.
March 1997 - Russian parliament approves amnesty for most Chechen rebel fighters.
April 1997 - At least four people die in two bomb blasts in the southern Russia. Moscow and the Chechen government pin the blame on "parties of war" which want to wreck the peace process.
May 10, 1997 - A Russian television crew is kidnapped in Chechnya, two days ahead of the Yeltsin-Maskhadov meeting.
May 12 1997 - Yeltsin and Maskhadov sign the peace accord.
